title: Grade 2 Math — Mon, Jun 09
description: Measurement — Day 1 of 5: Units of length (cm, m, km)
subject: mathematics

questions.question: Which unit do we use to measure the length of a pencil?
questions.explanation: A pencil is a small object. We measure small lengths in centimetres (cm).

questions.question: Which unit is used to measure the length of a room?
questions.explanation: A room is bigger than a pencil. We use metres (m) for bigger lengths.

questions.question: The distance from Delhi to Lucknow is about 500 ___.
questions.explanation: Very long distances between cities are measured in kilometres (km).

questions.question: A thumbnail is about 1 ___ wide.
questions.explanation: A thumbnail is very small — it is about 1 centimetre wide.

questions.question: Which is the shortest unit of the three?
questions.explanation: Centimetre is the shortest. 100 cm = 1 m; 1000 m = 1 km.

questions.question: A cricket pitch is 20 ___ long.
questions.explanation: A cricket pitch is about 20 metres — longer than a room but much shorter than a kilometre.

questions.question: How many centimetres are in 1 metre?
questions.explanation: 1 metre = 100 centimetres. Think of a metre ruler with 100 small divisions.

questions.question: A book is 25 ___ thick.
questions.explanation: A book is a small object. Its thickness is measured in centimetres.

questions.question: Which tool do we use to measure length?
questions.explanation: A ruler has centimetre markings and is used to measure length.

questions.question: The height of a tall building is measured in ___.
questions.explanation: Buildings are several metres tall. We use metres (m) to measure their height.

questions.question: Which is LONGEST?
questions.explanation: 1 km = 1000 m = 100,000 cm. Kilometre is the longest.

questions.question: A caterpillar is about 4 ___ long.
questions.explanation: A caterpillar is tiny — only a few centimetres long.

questions.question: Riya's school is 2 ___ from her house.
questions.explanation: The distance between two places is measured in kilometres.

questions.question: A door is about 2 ___ tall.
questions.explanation: A door is about 2 metres tall — much taller than your ruler but not as far as a kilometre.

questions.question: Which unit would you use to measure a football field?
questions.explanation: A football field is about 100 metres long. We use metres, not km (too far) or cm (too small).
